mechanism: The engine table is built from Horizons sub-points. The sub-solar point carries the apparent correction, so the Sun matches apparent directions to 0.0002 deg. The sub-Earth point is geometric, so the Earth differs from apparent directions by the aberration amount.
method: The Sun-Earth angle is invariant under rotation, so it compares the engine table (MOON_ME, body-fixed) against Horizons GEOMETRIC vectors (mean equator/node frame) without knowing the rotation between the frames. VECTORS epochs are TDB; converted to UTC with TDB-UTC = 69.184 s (32.184 s + 37 leap seconds). A direct vector comparison is meaningless: the two frames drift apart at the Moon's spin rate (13.18 deg/day).
openRefinement: The angle difference (0.007-0.008 deg) sits ~0.001-0.002 deg above pure aberration (0.0057 deg max); that excess is not yet separated. It does not change the verdict: the Earth residual is the known apparent correction, and the engine is geometrically consistent.
summary: The Earth direction error against Horizons apparent azimuth/elevation (max 0.00606 deg, vs 0.0002 deg for the Sun) is the apparent-vs-geometric difference, dominated by stellar aberration — not an engine error. Verified by a frame-free test: the Sun-Earth angle from the engine table differs from Horizons geometric VECTORS by 0.00697-0.00801 deg over 2027-01-01, the aberration magnitude. Light-time for Earth's motion contributes only ~0.0002 deg and cannot explain it.
